verifications.claim: The Automated Ball-Strike (ABS) Challenge System starts with the 2026 MLB season.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "for the 2026 Major League Baseball season"; "Beginning with Wednesday night's ... 2026 MLB season opener"; "Beginning with the 2026 MLB season"; "2026/03/25"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the system debuts or begins in the 2026 MLB season.

verifications.claim: The ABS Challenge System allows players to immediately appeal home plate umpire calls.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "challenge calls at the plate"; "appeal the ball and strike calls made by plate umpires"; "challenge a ball or strike call"; "appeal the strike-zone judgments of human home-plate umpires"
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe the system as allowing players to challenge or appeal umpire ball/strike calls.

verifications.claim: Players (pitcher, catcher, or batter) challenge by tapping their helmet/hat.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "a batter, pitcher, or catcher can formally make a challenge"; "the pitcher, catcher or hitter can challenge ... by tapping his helmet or hat"; "A pitcher, catcher or batter can challenge ... by tapping his hat or helmet"; "The player taps his cap or helmet"
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state that only pitcher, catcher, or batter can challenge by tapping helmet/hat.

verifications.claim: Tapping their helmet/hat prompts a Hawkeye-camera replay.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "tapping his helmet or hat. The umpire will acknowledge the challenge and the pitch will then be replayed"; "Statcast (and now ABS) has been powered by Hawk-Eye cameras ... five Hawk-Eye cameras are specifically committed to tracking the movement of the baseball"
verifications.reasoning: Challenge signal (tap) leads to replay/animation from Hawk-Eye camera system.

verifications.claim: Teams start with two challenges per game, as ESPN states.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Each team will get two challenges to start the game."
verifications.reasoning: ESPN source (R2) directly states teams start with two challenges per game.

verifications.claim: Successful challenges lead to no loss of a challenge, as ESPN states.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If a team wins a challenge, it can keep challenging."
verifications.reasoning: ESPN source (R2) directly states teams retain challenges if successful.

verifications.claim: If a challenge is initiated, the pitch is immediately replayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "transmitted within seconds"; "the pitch will then be replayed in real time via animation"; "Within seconds, the result is displayed"; "nearly instantaneously shown"
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm pitch location is replayed/shown in real time or within seconds upon challenge.

verifications.claim: The replay shows the precise location relative to the batter's specific height-calibrated strike zone.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "monitors each pitch location relative to the batter’s strike zone"; "tracks the precise location of each pitch, relative to the specific batter’s zone, which is calibrated to his height"; "monitors the exact location of each pitch, relative to the specific batter’s zone"; "each player has their zone measured ... 53.5% of their measured height"
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe replay/graphic showing precise pitch location in batter-specific, height-based strike zone.

verifications.claim: The replay is shown on the stadium scoreboard.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "to both the in-stadium video board"; "on the stadium videoboard"; "on the stadium video board"; "shown to those in attendance via the videoboard"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state the replay/graphic is shown on stadium video board/scoreboard.

verifications.claim: Only the batter, pitcher, or catcher can initiate a challenge within seconds of the call, says Facebook.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No cited reference attributes this to Facebook or mentions Facebook; attribution unsupported by provided sources.

verifications.claim: The ABS Challenge System was extensively tested in Minor League Baseball before the 2026 MLB season implementation, says Netflix.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "ABS has been tested in the Minor Leagues"
verifications.reasoning: Netflix source (R1) confirms testing in Minor Leagues before 2026, but does not use 'extensively'; other sources imply extent but attribution is to Netflix.

verifications.claim: The ABS Challenge System was extensively tested in MLB Spring Training before the 2026 MLB season implementation, says Netflix.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "ABS has been tested ... in Major League Spring Training"
verifications.reasoning: Netflix source (R1) confirms testing in MLB Spring Training before 2026, but does not use 'extensively'; other sources imply extent but attribution is to Netflix.
